why: Hand-authored situational practice items for ALL twelve A1.1 Lektionen. The first DaF review of 2026-09-12 measured the legacy grammar bank as drill rather than situation (L10 drew 0 of 7 items containing a Wortfeld word, L12 2, L6 3, L5 4) and the second review measured what the first batch left open: L9 3/7, L3 3/7, L11 3/7, L2 4/7, L4 4/7, plus L8 drawing two unsolvable ordinal-number items and L1/L7 leaning on words the Lektion never uses. Every item here uses the exact Wortfeld of its Lektion (src/data/curricula/a11.js, read only) plus earlier Lektionen, is typed production (fill_blank without options, sentence_building or error_correction), is German-only in prompt and answer, and passes src/data/lessonPools/quality.js. THREE RULES the second review asked for, applied to every item: (1) the answer follows unambiguously from the GERMAN prompt — where several verbs fit a gap the prompt carries the infinitive cue „(fahren)“, and where several forms are correct they are all in `accepted` (extra-a11-l10-01 now accepts Fährt/Geht/Kommt, as its own Lektion pretest does); (2) `accepted` carries the lowercase variant only where the gap is sentence-initial — the höfliche „Ihr“ and the mid-sentence „ein/eine/sein“ are case-strict, because capitalisation is the taught distinction; (3) every task instruction uses Sie („Bilden Sie die Frage“, „Korrigieren Sie“, „Schreiben Sie“), matching the course, while the dialogues keep du between friends (review §C). Intonation questions are no longer marked wrong: the two error_correction items on „Der Zug fährt nach …?“ now ask for the WRITTEN question form. scripts/build-lesson-pool.mjs merges this file into a11.json under the same filter; tests/lesson-extra-items.test.mjs pins the Wortfeld hit and the resulting draw. ROUND 3 (REVIEW-daf-3-2026-09-12): the hand-authored batch was itself reviewed and corrected — L11 lost three NON-separable verbs (frühstücken/duschen/schlafen) from the Satzklammer Lektion and gained abholen/mitkommen/anrufen; three L3 items drilled possessive endings (L12) and the Vokalwechsel du-form sprichst (deferred to L7) under a personal-pronouns label and are now genuine pronoun items; two L2 number-spelling items tagged verb-sein are now sein items; L7 no longer demands Samstag (taught in L8) and L8 no longer Vormittag (taught nowhere); L10 asks for the normal word order instead of calling a marked question an error; every gap whose answer is a verb carries its infinitive in the GERMAN prompt, and no English gloss carries a bracket the German prompt lacks. The rule behind the round: a topic mark is a routing label, so tests/lesson-extra-items.test.mjs now measures what the ANSWER drills, per Lektion. ROUND 6 (REVIEW-daf-5-2026-09-12): extra-a11-l05-08 no longer punishes the answer its own task formula demands — the prompt lost the „das“ that stood before the gap („Ist hier ein Heft? — Ja, und ___ Heft ist grün.“) and the key is the bare article the cue asks for, which is what the new `cueAnswerMismatch` rule in quality.js pins for the whole pool. `caseSensitive` is now set where the TASK is the capital letter and nowhere else: extra-a11-l01-06, l03-08, l12-08, l12-09 and l12-16 carry it and their explanations name the capital; extra-a11-l12-10 („sie, Plural“ → ihre) LOST it, because there the capital is only the sentence opening — the rule is „flag iff the explanation says the capital letter is the point“, and tests/lesson-extra-items.test.mjs pins both directions. Lektion 10 now makes the learner PRODUCE the inversion in six items (l10-07/08/09/12/13/14) rather than fill a gap in front of a question mark the prompt already carries; their task formulas are varied on purpose, because buildLesson.js caps any lemma at MAX_SAME_LEMMA=2 and eight prompts saying „Frage“ would have let two of them be drawn. Lektion 2 gained the four number items the review asked for (l02-09..12: the digit stands in the prompt cue, the learner writes the word) — they carry `topic: verb-sein` because the closed slug list of scripts/validate-curriculum.mjs has no numbers slug, so verb-sein is the routing label that reaches Lektion 2; they do NOT drill sein and drillsSlug says so. Lektion 9 gained l09-09 („Fragen Sie höflich im Café: ___ Sie auch Kuchen? (haben)“). No explanation claims a percentage, „immer“ or „ohne Ausnahme“ any more (MAJOR 7), and the test suite forbids all three. ROUND 7 (REVIEW-daf-6-2026-09-12): Lektion 4 grew from eight items to twelve (l04-09..12), because with eight it filled three to four of its seven drawn places from the legacy bank and drew Genus at Instrument, Freiheit, Zeitung, Sonne and Kaffee — words no Lektion of the course introduces; the four new items use nothing but L4's own Wortfeld (Flohmarkt, Lampe, Stuhl, Uhr, kosten, Euro, die Zahlen 11–100) and earlier Lektionen, and the review's own draft of l04-09 („am Samstag“) and l04-11 („aber billig“) was corrected here because Samstag is taught in L8 and billig in no Lektion at all (RULE 11 lexis). extra-a11-l05-09 now NAMES its task („(mit bestimmtem Artikel)“): the quote „Ein Schere ist hier.“ has exactly one error and „Eine Schere ist hier.“ is the minimal repair, so without the cue the model answer punished a correct sentence — the pool-wide rule is the new `ambiguousCorrection` in quality.js and its mirror in tests/lesson-extra-items.test.mjs: a correction may differ from its quote only in the way the German prompt names. extra-a11-l10-06 no longer accepts Gehst/gehst — „Gehst du morgen mit dem Bus?“ is not German, one goes BY bus (fahren, kommen) and not WITH it, and the fahren/gehen/kommen family is therefore frame-dependent rather than per-lemma. The four L2 number items moved from `topic: verb-sein` to `topic: numbers`: under verb-sein a misspelled number word was tagged „Konjugation“ and answered with more sein drills. The topic is a routing label, so it only reaches Lektion 2 once L2's `practiceRule.topics` lists `numbers` — that half of the fix lives in src/data/curricula/a11.js and scripts/validate-curriculum.mjs, not here. Two RULE 11b offenders (the new drawn-lexis rule: a word is measured at the Lektion the item is actually DRAWN in, not at the earliest Lektion that could draw it) were hand-written and are fixed here: extra-a11-l01-07 dropped the ss-respelling „Ich heisse Ana.“ from `accepted` — checkAnswer is ß/ss-blind, so the variant never did any work and only put an untaught token in the pool — and extra-a11-l05-10 asks for „Das Bild ist gelb.“ instead of „schön“, which Lektion 12 teaches, while gelb is one of Lektion 5's own colours. ROUND 10 (worker R10-F): the fresh-per-attempt draw made attempt 3 the honest test, and four Lektionen fell under PRIMARY_MIN on it — L3 0/7, L10 2/7, L2 and L9 3/7 — because three attempts need twelve fresh REAL producers per Lektion and the pool held eight to fifteen. Fourteen items close that as supply rather than as a looser predicate: four L3 pronoun producers (es/wir/ihr/er, l03-09..12), two L2 sein producers (bist/seid, l02-13/14), two L9 haben producers (hat/hast, l09-10/11), three L10 items whose ANSWER is the whole inverted question (l10-17..19) and three L4 Genus items WITHOUT a price (l04-19..21) — L4 held 18 eligible items of which nine say kostet/Euro, so no seven existed under MAX_SAME_LEMMA with distinct task shapes and the draw had to relax the lemma cap; with a Tisch, a Rucksack and a plural item in three unused shapes it fills seven under every cap and MAX_CAP_STARVED_LEKTIONEN in tests/lesson-engine.test.mjs is 0. Every new item carries a task shape its Lektion does not already use (measured with `taskShape`, src/lib/lesson/buildLesson.js). Six items were REWORDED rather than dropped: each carried a word the course never teaches, so scripts/build-lesson-pool.mjs stamped `minLektion: null` and no Lektion could ever serve them — liegt (l05-02), offen (l05-05), klein (l05-07 and l12-04), Januar (l12-11) and richtig (l10-03) gave way to words their own Lektion teaches. ROUND 11 (worker R11-A, DaF review #10 MAJOR 1 and 2): the task-shape key stopped counting wording. A spelled-letter sequence is ONE token (five letter-for-letter identical L1 prompts counted as five „shapes“ because every letter entered the skeleton as its own `·`), a bracketed instruction is its CATEGORY from the closed `TASK_MARKS` set (the six L10 items of round 10 were one task in six wordings), a scrambled word list is its length class, and an adjective is content even where `LEMMA_STOPWORDS` holds it. Re-measured against that key, four Lektionen could no longer fill seven distinct shapes with four real drills across all three attempts, so this batch grew by 54 items in task shapes their Lektion did not already own: L1 +14 (spell-the-name, letter-name lookup, two more greeting corrections, two word-list sentences — L1 held eight shapes and needs seven per draw, three draws deep), L4 +20 (price-free Genus frames — „Ich kaufe ___“, „Was kostet ___“, „Hier ist ___“, plurals, and three article corrections whose answer is a whole sentence — because L4 has only three answer keys and `MAX_SAME_ANSWER_KEY` is two), L6 +10 (indefinite-article corrections and word lists WITHOUT the „(unbestimmter Artikel)“ cue, which `MAX_SAME_LEMMA` counts as the lemma `artikel`) and L8 +10 (um/am with a clock time, the weekday sequence, two more preposition corrections). `extra-a11-l10-17`…`-22` were REWRITTEN rather than added: three turn a quoted statement into a question, three write the question that belongs to a given „Ja, …“ answer — and neither wording says „Frage“, which is what the lemma cap was really counting in L10. `extra-a11-l06-06` lost „Ich habe … für dich“ (both words are untaught at L6 under the round-11 lexicon) and now reads „Die Chefin braucht ___ Handynummer.“. Measured after the round: all 36 blocks fill seven items in seven distinct task shapes with at least four real drills, every lemma ≤ 2, every answer key ≤ 2, `relaxUsed` 0 everywhere, and consecutive attempts (1→2, 2→3 AND the wrap pair 3→1) share nothing except L8's two `mustCover` items and L12's polite „Ihr“. ROUND 12 (worker R12-D, DaF review #11 MAJOR 1(b), the last open block): attempt 3 of L5 was the one block still reporting `complete: false` — of the 17 `definite-articles` items it could serve, attempts 1 and 2 used eleven and the six left over were ALL the frame „___ Nomen ist Adjektiv. (bestimmter Artikel)“, which `MAX_SAME_TASK_SHAPE` seats once, so the seven filled up from L4's flea market. `extra-a11-l05-17`…`-24` are eight items out of L5's own Kursraum-Wortfeld in eight task shapes L5 did not own (the indefinite→definite pair „Ein Bild ist hier. ___ Bild ist blau.“, „Wie ist ___ Tür? — Sie ist weiß.“, „Ergänzen Sie: Ist ___ Lineal hier?“, a two-noun frame, a quoted question and a Zimmer frame, plus two article corrections whose answer is a whole sentence). Attempt 3 now seats five items on its own slug instead of one and its Wortfeld share rose 2/7 → 5/7; `MAX_OFF_PRIMARY_BLOCKS` in tests/lesson-engine.test.mjs is 0. ROUND 15 (worker R15-A, DaF review #14 MAJOR 2): every error_correction whose one-token repair changes an ARTICLE or a POSSESSIVE now NAMES the element in the German prompt — the five L6 items, l09-07 („Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: …“) and l12-15/l12-16 („… den Possessivartikel: …“). The reason is the class, not the ids: for ANY article correction a noun of another gender that fits the slot is a second, equally minimal repair — „Ihre Papa kommt auch.“ is repaired by „Ihr Papa“ and just as well by „Ihre Mama“, and „die Mama“/„der Papa“ as well as „das Fest“/„die Party“ stand as neighbouring Wortfeld lines of the very Lektion that serves the item. No partner table can enumerate that (Mama/Papa is suppletive, Fest/Party is no derivation at all), so the convention replaces the proof: `missingDeterminerCue` in quality.js is the rule, scripts/build-lesson-pool.mjs injects the cue into any cache prompt that lacks it (task wording, never the answer key), and tests/lesson-extra-items.test.mjs measures the built pool AND all four checkpoints rather than a list of ids.
